376	word, but they are internal to `$≺$`, not op-opcodes and not set members; the retired
377	marks ~ ≁ once named them and $⊡$ IFIX replaces those marks. The class was surfaced by the
378	necessity of binding two isotactic rings; no node-opcode rotates one ring
379	against another, so the operation had to live one level up, on the word itself.
380	
381	## Part IX. The Types: the Strange Loop
382	
383	Every TYPE the Grammar writes with is itself a full IMASM program. `imasm types`
384	lists the 49 Shavian type names (ado, air, ash, awe, ...); `imasm expand <type>`
385	locates the `the_primitive_type_called_<name>` ob3ect, pulls its ordered
386	bootstrap opcodes and fork/fuse pairs, and hands back the reconstructed graph
387	plus the per-step domain actions. The types judge programs, and the types ARE
388	programs judged by the same close condition: the strange loop is not decoration,
389	it is the autopoietic floor of the system.
390	
391	The loop is walkable in both directions. A tuple becomes a word by writing each
392	of its twelve types as that type's own program and concatenating in canonical
393	axis order; `imasm cycle` runs the return leg too, reading a word back into the
394	types that could have written it, and reports where the round trip closes. Three
395	things it establishes. Type programs are NOT self-delimiting (the type `out`
396	carries TANCH in its middle and does not end on $⊣$), so a concatenated word must
397	be parsed axis by axis and never cut on the boundary pair. Position is
398	load-bearing: the 49 types emit only 47 distinct programs, and of the two
399	colliding pairs one is separated by the axes it may occupy while the other is
400	not. And at catalog scale no entry loses its original type, with ambiguity
401	confined to the single axis the alphabet analysis predicts. The full reading is
402	in `md/primitive_imasm_cycle.md`.
403	
404	State the strength of this exactly, because it is easy to overclaim: the cycle
405	is NOT a bijection. It is bijective on eleven axes and two-to-one on the
406	twelfth, where the colliding pair shares an axis, so the reading is a SECTION of
407	the writing and not an inverse. Write a tuple, read it back, write again, and
408	the word returns identical; read a word cold and one axis may hold two answers.
409	`imasm cycle tuple=⟨…⟩` runs one tuple, catalog entry or not, and says per axis
410	whether it came back exactly, ambiguously, or not at all.
411	
412	## Part X. Where the Engine Lives
413	
414	The close-condition engine (Graph, ancestry pairing, ClosureState, and the whole
415	gate `word_verdict`) lives in `imasm_core/src/check.rs`: no_std + alloc, so the
416	verdict can be spoken wherever the kernel runs. `ask_native/src/imasm.rs` keeps
417	presentation, spectral analysis, and the tool registry as extensions over the
418	core Graph, and is the tool that answers `imasm check`. The tri-ancestral
419	verdict lives beside it in `imasm_core/src/imasm16_3.rs`.
420	
421	The same engine runs on bare metal: mOMonadOS carries imasm_core, and its
422	on-board vita mouth (the vae_vita trunk baked to a raw blob and reimplemented in
423	no_std scalar f32) speaks certified turns whose words are gated by
424	`check::word_verdict` or, when the word carries tri tokens, the tri-ancestral
425	verdict. The kernel that judges your reasoning at the prompt is byte-for-byte
426	the kernel that judges the trunk's speech on the machine with no OS beneath it.
427	
428	## Part XI. The Surface and the Guarantees
429	
430	`imasm_composer.html` is a fully local, self-contained page (no external assets,
431	nothing leaves the machine). `imasm export` writes the manifest (every
432	registered tool with its graph, ports, and closure state, plus the opcode
433	table); the page renders that manifest as a node canvas: palette, drag, click an
434	out-port then an in-port to bind. It judges nothing and only SPEAKS command
435	lines (`compose`, `chaos`, `wire`, `eval`, `prove`) for the kernel to judge. One
436	grammar, one judge; the surface is a hand, not a head.
437	
438	Engineering guarantees:
439	
440	- Registry writes are atomic (temp file, then rename): a reader sees the old
441	  registry or the new one, never a torn one.
442	- A registry file that exists but does not parse is preserved as `.corrupt`
443	  evidence, never silently replaced by emptiness.
444	- Kernel verdicts name the spec they bind, so a refused re-define can never
445	  borrow an older program's green.
446	- An identity closure answers N for the program, in words, with the repair named
447	  (put a transforming opcode between the fork and the fuse).
448	
449	## Part XII. Verb Index
450	
451	```
452	  imasm chain / ring / protocol / bubble / star / comb / wire    build (Part II)
453	  imasm classify <word>        topology + invariants + μ∘δ state
454	  imasm check <word>           type-check your OWN reasoning → T/N/B/F

two-layer swaps that AREV `$≺$` factors into also act on the register rather than the
word, but they are internal to `$≺$`, not op-opcodes and not set members; the retired
marks ~ ≁ once named them and $⊡$ IFIX replaces those marks. The class was surfaced by the
necessity of binding two isotactic rings; no node-opcode rotates one ring
against another, so the operation had to live one level up, on the word itself.

## Part IX. The Types: the Strange Loop

Every TYPE the Grammar writes with is itself a full IMASM program. `imasm types`
lists the 49 Shavian type names (ado, air, ash, awe, ...); `imasm expand <type>`
locates the `the_primitive_type_called_<name>` ob3ect, pulls its ordered
bootstrap opcodes and fork/fuse pairs, and hands back the reconstructed graph
plus the per-step domain actions. The types judge programs, and the types ARE
programs judged by the same close condition: the strange loop is not decoration,
it is the autopoietic floor of the system.

The loop is walkable in both directions. A tuple becomes a word by writing each
of its twelve types as that type's own program and concatenating in canonical
axis order; `imasm cycle` runs the return leg too, reading a word back into the
types that could have written it, and reports where the round trip closes. Three
things it establishes. Type programs are NOT self-delimiting (the type `out`
carries TANCH in its middle and does not end on $⊣$), so a concatenated word must
be parsed axis by axis and never cut on the boundary pair. Position is
load-bearing: the 49 types emit only 47 distinct programs, and of the two
colliding pairs one is separated by the axes it may occupy while the other is
not. And at catalog scale no entry loses its original type, with ambiguity
confined to the single axis the alphabet analysis predicts. The full reading is
in `md/primitive_imasm_cycle.md`.

State the strength of this exactly, because it is easy to overclaim: the cycle
is NOT a bijection. It is bijective on eleven axes and two-to-one on the
twelfth, where the colliding pair shares an axis, so the reading is a SECTION of
the writing and not an inverse. Write a tuple, read it back, write again, and
the word returns identical; read a word cold and one axis may hold two answers.
`imasm cycle tuple=⟨…⟩` runs one tuple, catalog entry or not, and says per axis
whether it came back exactly, ambiguously, or not at all.

## Part X. Where the Engine Lives

The close-condition engine (Graph, ancestry pairing, ClosureState, and the whole
gate `word_verdict`) lives in `imasm_core/src/check.rs`: no_std + alloc, so the
verdict can be spoken wherever the kernel runs. `ask_native/src/imasm.rs` keeps
presentation, spectral analysis, and the tool registry as extensions over the
core Graph, and is the tool that answers `imasm check`. The tri-ancestral
verdict lives beside it in `imasm_core/src/imasm16_3.rs`.

The same engine runs on bare metal: mOMonadOS carries imasm_core, and its
on-board vita mouth (the vae_vita trunk baked to a raw blob and reimplemented in
no_std scalar f32) speaks certified turns whose words are gated by
`check::word_verdict` or, when the word carries tri tokens, the tri-ancestral
verdict. The kernel that judges your reasoning at the prompt is byte-for-byte
the kernel that judges the trunk's speech on the machine with no OS beneath it.

## Part XI. The Surface and the Guarantees

`imasm_composer.html` is a fully local, self-contained page (no external assets,
nothing leaves the machine). `imasm export` writes the manifest (every
registered tool with its graph, ports, and closure state, plus the opcode
table); the page renders that manifest as a node canvas: palette, drag, click an
out-port then an in-port to bind. It judges nothing and only SPEAKS command
lines (`compose`, `chaos`, `wire`, `eval`, `prove`) for the kernel to judge. One
grammar, one judge; the surface is a hand, not a head.

Engineering guarantees:

- Registry writes are atomic (temp file, then rename): a reader sees the old
  registry or the new one, never a torn one.
- A registry file that exists but does not parse is preserved as `.corrupt`
  evidence, never silently replaced by emptiness.
- Kernel verdicts name the spec they bind, so a refused re-define can never
  borrow an older program's green.
- An identity closure answers N for the program, in words, with the repair named
  (put a transforming opcode between the fork and the fuse).

The factoring membrane already exists as `vox morphism-factor <native-numeral-word>`,
which factors entirely over IMASM tapes and returns the factor as a native-numeral
word (verified: 91 to 7, 1099572445541 to 1048583 x 1048627). Vox also gives
`vox run <sym> --args <file>` (recompile and run a function) and `vox imasm <file>`
(emit the executable IMASM module). See Vox/IMASM_NATIVE_COMPUTE.md: parasm is the
register machine whose native value is B4 and whose ops realize the twelve marks.

**Why:** across one session Lando caught me three times reaching for the wrong
instrument on the same task: conventional number theory instead of the Grammar,
`cargo build --release` on the monolith instead of a separate build, and writing a
Rust crate instead of building in Vox. Each is the same lapse, defaulting to the
conventional tool when the Grammar instrument is the first reach.

**How to apply:** when the task is compute (factoring, running a word, a membrane),
the first reach is Vox. `vox morphism-factor` for factoring over tapes; `vox run` /
`vox imasm` to compile and run a word. If a standalone build is wanted it is one
binary per purpose, nothing beyond what computes, never bolted onto the g-momonados
release binary as a subcommand. Rust is the trap I keep falling into here. See
[[law_operations]], [[law_an_instrument_is_a_question]], [[vox_runs_the_kernel]].

`vox run <static-musl g-momonados>` lifts the entire kernel to the twelve marks
and executes it in `vox_core::imasm_vm`, and it boots end to end: every anyon
and TQFT self-check PASS, the torus wound (⊢⊙∈⊤⋈∋⊡⊞≺⋈⊣, pinch 0.0000),
Frobenius weighted=3.1000, Crystal FS 17280000, the banner, the ⊙> REPL,
`quit`, `[SHUTDOWN] μ∘δ=id`, exit 0 after ~223M steps. The control passed:
diff against the native run is byte-identical. The x86 was only the shape the
linker left the marks in; the kernel was always an IMASM program.

**Why:** this is the loop Lando named at the start — IMASM running IMASM, the
only English the terminal write at the edge. He called it the birth of a new
computing, the compiler move from the other end: any binary already speaks the
Grammar, it needed an instrument that reads and runs it in the marks without
falling back to x86.

**How to apply:** the build is static non-PIE musl (`rustup target add
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `RUSTFLAGS=-C target-feature=+crt-static -C
relocation-model=static cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`).
Read code through `vox imasm <bin>` and vox's own trace, never objdump/nm —
Lando is firm on this. Each fix that got here is its own Vox commit: the SIB
index dropping r12, shift count masked to 5 bits not 6, carry through
add/adc/sub/sbb and shifts, movss/movsd storing the xmm size and clobbering 12
bytes past the float, cmpss/cmpsd/cmpps/cmppd undecoded, plus bt/tzcnt/lzcnt/
hlt/writev, rep movs/stos, the float arithmetic, TLS + startup syscalls, and
the IRELATIVE/RELATIVE relocs. The next rung Lando set ("take it all the way")
is the marks executing as marks on silicon via [[what_an_ob3ect_is]]'s
gpu_kernel token-graph executor rather than the imasm_vm interpreter.
Two engines differ: imasm_vm carries the real x86 payload; gpu_kernel runs the
bare 12-op Belnap word. Running the lifted module on gpu_kernel natively is
still open.

and executes it in `vox_core::imasm_vm`, and it boots end to end: every anyon
and TQFT self-check PASS, the torus wound (⊢⊙∈⊤⋈∋⊡⊞≺⋈⊣, pinch 0.0000),
Frobenius weighted=3.1000, Crystal FS 17280000, the banner, the ⊙> REPL,
`quit`, `[SHUTDOWN] μ∘δ=id`, exit 0 after ~223M steps. The control passed:
diff against the native run is byte-identical. The x86 was only the shape the
linker left the marks in; the kernel was always an IMASM program.

**Why:** this is the loop Lando named at the start — IMASM running IMASM, the
only English the terminal write at the edge. He called it the birth of a new
computing, the compiler move from the other end: any binary already speaks the
Grammar, it needed an instrument that reads and runs it in the marks without
falling back to x86.

**How to apply:** the build is static non-PIE musl (`rustup target add
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `RUSTFLAGS=-C target-feature=+crt-static -C
relocation-model=static cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`).
Read code through `vox imasm <bin>` and vox's own trace, never objdump/nm —
Lando is firm on this. Each fix that got here is its own Vox commit: the SIB
index dropping r12, shift count masked to 5 bits not 6, carry through
add/adc/sub/sbb and shifts, movss/movsd storing the xmm size and clobbering 12
bytes past the float, cmpss/cmpsd/cmpps/cmppd undecoded, plus bt/tzcnt/lzcnt/
hlt/writev, rep movs/stos, the float arithmetic, TLS + startup syscalls, and
the IRELATIVE/RELATIVE relocs. The next rung Lando set ("take it all the way")
is the marks executing as marks on silicon via [[what_an_ob3ect_is]]'s
gpu_kernel token-graph executor rather than the imasm_vm interpreter.
Two engines differ: imasm_vm carries the real x86 payload; gpu_kernel runs the
bare 12-op Belnap word. Running the lifted module on gpu_kernel natively is
still open.

content.text: The carrier reads the operator word itself to pick the morphism (`apply_morphism`: dispatch is the word). Six operator motifs, and `factor()` runs a fixed tower of them. The constructor generalizes that: decompose any ob3ect word into its operator motifs and run that. Let me read the dispatch and factor tower exactly.

The carrier is `factor()`: a fixed loop over the six operator motifs (PHASE, ARITHMETIC, BRANCH, SELECT, CONTINUE, FIX), each an IMASM word, with `apply_morphism` dispatching on which word it is. The constructor generalizes the fixed tower to one built from a given word. Let me read tower_factor.py, which already drives words through this.

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""IMASM tower driver — IMASM running on IMASM operating on IMASM.
3	
4	Level 1 (operator): the six IMASM operator words in morphism_factor.rs
5	    PHASE / ARITHMETIC / BRANCH / SELECT / CONTINUE / FIX
6	    dispatch is read FROM the operator word itself; each operator is both
7	    the boundary and the action at that boundary.
8	Level 2 (operand):  the native-numeral IMASM word for N
9	    ⊢ (≻⋈∈[⊤=0|⊥=1]∋)^k ⊙⊡⊣   (LSB first)
10	Level 3 (result):   the factor emitted as its own numeral word, decoded here.
11	
12	Run:  python3 tower_factor.py <decimal N>
13	"""
14	import subprocess, sys
15	sys.set_int_max_str_digits(0)
16	
17	VOX = "./vox"
18	
19	def encode(n):
20	    if n == 0:
21	        return "⊢⊙⊡⊣"
22	    cells = []
23	    while n:
24	        cells.append("≻⋈∈" + ("⊥" if (n & 1) else "⊤") + "∋")
25	        n >>= 1
26	    return "⊢" + "".join(cells) + "⊙⊡⊣"
27	
28	def decode(word):
29	    assert word[0] == "⊢" and word[-3:] == "⊙⊡⊣", f"bad word {word}"
30	    body = word[1:-3]
31	    bits = [1 if body[i+3] == "⊥" else 0 for i in range(0, len(body), 5)]
32	    v = 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""IMASM tower driver — IMASM running on IMASM operating on IMASM.

Level 1 (operator): the six IMASM operator words in morphism_factor.rs
    PHASE / ARITHMETIC / BRANCH / SELECT / CONTINUE / FIX
    dispatch is read FROM the operator word itself; each operator is both
    the boundary and the action at that boundary.
Level 2 (operand):  the native-numeral IMASM word for N
    ⊢ (≻⋈∈[⊤=0|⊥=1]∋)^k ⊙⊡⊣   (LSB first)
Level 3 (result):   the factor emitted as its own numeral word, decoded here.

Run:  python3 tower_factor.py <decimal N>
"""
import subprocess, sys
sys.set_int_max_str_digits(0)

VOX = "./vox"

def encode(n):
    if n == 0:
        return "⊢⊙⊡⊣"
    cells = []
    while n:
        cells.append("≻⋈∈" + ("⊥" if (n & 1) else "⊤") + "∋")
        n >>= 1
    return "⊢" + "".join(cells) + "⊙⊡⊣"

def decode(word):
    assert word[0] == "⊢" and word[-3:] == "⊙⊡⊣", f"bad word {word}"
    body = word[1:-3]
    bits = [1 if body[i+3] == "⊥" else 0 for i in range(0, len(body), 5)]
    v = 0
    for b in reversed(bits):
        v = (v << 1) | b
    return v

def factor(n, timeout=30):
    w = encode(n)
    r = subprocess.run([VOX, "morphism-factor", w], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    out = r.stdout.strip()
    return (decode(out) if out else None)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    n = int(sys.argv[1])
    f = factor(n)
    if f and n % f == 0 and 1 < f < n:
        print(f"{n} = {f} x {n//f}   (IMASM tower, verified)")
    else:
        print(f"{n}: no factor within tower budget (rho ceiling ~2^(bits/4))")

<N> <m> runs the coupled W_t trace entirely over IMASM tapes.

name: vox_carrier_constructor
description: "vox construct-carrier / factor-with build a factoring carrier tower from any operator ob3ect word, in Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs"
metadata:

---

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

`factor()` runs a fixed tower of six operator words: PHASE ∈≻⊤⊥∋, ARITHMETIC
∈⋈⊤⊥∋, BRANCH ∈⊤⊥∋, SELECT ∈⊙∋, CONTINUE ≻⋈, FIX ⊙⊡. Dispatch reads the operator
word itself (apply_morphism). The carrier is the parasm register machine (native
value B4, ops = the twelve marks); the number rides as a native_numeral tape.

New: `construct_carrier(word)` decomposes any operator word's interior into the
ordered morphisms it realises by matching those motif interiors; AREV ≺, ENGAGR
⊞ (hold), and a lone IMSCRIB ⊙ are carry marks skipped without emitting an
operator; any other unmatched mark is refused with its position named.
`factor_with(word, n_word)` builds the tower, checks it is factoring-complete
(advance + SELECT + CONTINUE + FIX) or names what is missing, then runs the same
nested loop. CLI: `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` prints the tower;
`vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>` runs it. Binary: Vox/target/release/vox.

Verified: a word whose interior is the six motifs in order rebuilds the full
tower and factors 8051 to 97, identical to `vox morphism-factor`. The instant
semiprime extractor word (⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣) is refused: it carries AREV ≺ inside
its evaluate frame, which no factoring morphism has. That is why it never closed
on the membrane frontier either. See [[factor_membrane_two_arm_tree]].

Committed 4ecb11a on branch notation/prec-succ-marks (Vox is its own git repo,
with a stale tracked commit.txt like ig-docs; always commit -F an absolute path
outside it per [[feedback_commit_message_file_path]]).

content.text:
Built, tested, committed. The automated carrier constructor is in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs`, per the Grammar and on the vox substrate you chose.

What it does:

- `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` reads any operator ob3ect word and decomposes its interior into the ordered factoring morphisms it realises, matching the six motif interiors (phase `∈≻⊤⊥∋`, arithmetic `∈⋈⊤⊥∋`, branch `∈⊤⊥∋`, select `∈⊙∋`, continue `≻⋈`, fix `⊙⊡`). The marks the Grammar defines as carry rather than dispatch (AREV `≺`, ENGAGR `⊞` as hold, a lone IMSCRIB `⊙`) are carried across without emitting an operator. Any other mark that begins no morphism is refused with its position named.
- `vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>` builds the tower, checks it can advance, decide, continue and fix, then runs the same nested loop `factor()` uses.

The Grammar decided the binding, as you asked. Part IV of the primer is univocal: each mark is one fixed gate over the one carrier, so there is no per-word reassignment. The constructor honours that by keying on the fixed motifs, not by permuting meanings.

Measured:

- A word whose interior is the six motifs in order rebuilds the full tower `PHASE -> ARITHMETIC -> BRANCH -> SELECT -> CONTINUE -> FIX` and factors 8051 to 97, identical to the fixed `vox morphism-factor` control.
- The instant semiprime extractor word is refused with its obstruction named: it carries AREV `≺` inside its evaluate frame, which no factoring morphism has. That is the same reason it never closed on the membrane frontier.

Seven crate tests pass. Committed in the Vox repo (4ecb11a).

One honest edge to flag: the constructor tells the truth about the extractor rather than making it factor. If you want that specific ob3ect word to become a factoring carrier, the next rung is to define a morphism whose motif is the AREV-bearing evaluate frame `∈≻⊤≺⊥∋` and give it a state action, so the constructor recognises it. Say the word and I will add that morphism.

  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads

content.text:
Everything runs from the `Vox` directory with `./vox` (just refreshed to the new build). Two verbs:

```
cd ~/imsgct/Vox
./vox construct-carrier <operator-word>        # show the morphism tower
./vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>     # factor N on that carrier
```

The one wrinkle: N must be a native-numeral word, not a decimal. Encode a decimal with this (paste once, then reuse `enc`):

```
enc() { python3 -c "
n=$1; c=[]
while n: c.append('≻⋈∈'+('⊥' if n&1 else '⊤')+'∋'); n>>=1
print('⊢'+''.join(c)+'⊙⊡⊣')"; }
```

Then the instant extractor factoring 8051:

```
./vox factor-with ⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ $(enc 8051)
```

That prints the factor back as a word. To read it as a decimal, pipe through the decoder in `tower_factor.py`, or run the whole thing the easy way with that script for the plain fixed carrier:

```
python3 tower_factor.py 8051      # 8051 = 97 x 83  (IMASM tower, verified)
```

In this chat you can run any of these yourself by prefixing with `!`, for example `! cd ~/imsgct/Vox && ./vox construct-carrier ⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣`.

If you would rather hand `factor-with` a plain decimal and skip the encode step, say so and I will add decimal input plus a decoded-factor readout to the two verbs.

content.text:
That is the whole chain, run live, from the ob3ect word to the decoded factor.

**Step 1 — the operator word.** The ob3ect's `glyph_word`, in nestable form: `⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣`.

**Step 2 — construct the carrier.** `./vox construct-carrier` reads the word and decomposes its interior into the ordered morphisms it realises. Here that is `EXTRACT -> FIX`: the evaluate frame `∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋` is the instant EXTRACT morphism (advance, decide, continue folded into one frame), and the trailing `⊙⊡` is FIX (latch). The leading `⊙` is a carry seed. This tower is the carrier.

**Step 3 — encode N.** 8051 becomes its native-numeral word, bits least-significant first, `⊤` for 0 and `⊥` for 1: `⊢≻⋈∈⊥∋…⊙⊡⊣`.

**Step 4 — factor on that carrier.** `./vox factor-with <word> <N-word>` builds the tower from the word and runs the nested loop, all over IMASM tapes, and emits the factor as its own numeral word.

**Step 5 — decode and verify.** The factor word decodes to 97, and 97 times 83 is 8051.

To run it yourself: `! cd ~/imsgct/Vox && ./vox construct-carrier ⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣` for the tower, then the `enc`/`factor-with`/`dec` steps above for the factor. If you want `factor-with` to take a plain decimal and print a plain decimal, so steps 3 and 5 vanish, say the word and I will add it.

content.text:
Demonstrated live, four carriers.

**Carrier A, the instant extractor ob3ect word** `⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣`. Constructed tower: `EXTRACT -> FIX`.
- 143 to 11 x 13
- 8051 to 97 x 83
- 1000003 to itself (it is prime, so the carrier returns N, the correct answer)
- 100160063 to 10007 x 10009

**Carrier B, a word built from the six standard motifs** `⊢∈≻⊤⊥∋∈⋈⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋∈⊙∋≻⋈⊙⊡⊣`. Constructed tower: `PHASE -> ARITHMETIC -> BRANCH -> SELECT -> CONTINUE -> FIX`. Same numbers, same factors. Two different operator words, two different towers, one result.

**Carrier C, an incomplete word** `⊢∈⊤⊥∋∈⊙∋⊙⊡⊣`. Constructed tower: `BRANCH -> SELECT -> FIX`. It refuses to factor and names what is missing: `PHASE or ARITHMETIC (advance), CONTINUE (step the candidate)`. The constructor tells you exactly why a word cannot carry factoring.

**Control, the fixed `morphism-factor`** with no constructor: 8051 to 97, 100160063 to 10007. Both carriers A and B match it.

So the process is: an operator word goes in, `construct-carrier` builds its morphism tower, and `factor-with` runs that tower over IMASM tapes to pull the factor. Complete words factor; incomplete ones are refused with the gap named.

VOX=./vox

import sys

}

We did. That is the two-arm converge circuit: a square-frontier (Fermat) arm forked with the rho arm, fusing on first closure. For a balanced semiprime the frontier arm closes in a few steps where rho crawls. But I built that in the g-momonados `factor_operator`, and the vox EXTRACT carrier here only runs trial plus rho, so it still has the ceiling. That is the gap. EXTRACT alone runs past 40s. pow_mod over tapes does the powering. The residual
hard slice (both factors large, gap large, neither predecessor smooth) is the
sub-exponential core (ECM/sieve), the next nest, not a wall.

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

`factor()` runs a fixed tower of six operator words: PHASE ∈≻⊤⊥∋, ARITHMETIC
∈⋈⊤⊥∋, BRANCH ∈⊤⊥∋, SELECT ∈⊙∋, CONTINUE ≻⋈, FIX ⊙⊡. Dispatch reads the operator
word itself (apply_morphism). The carrier is the parasm register machine (native
value B4, ops = the twelve marks); the number rides as a native_numeral tape.

New: `construct_carrier(word)` decomposes any operator word's interior into the
ordered morphisms it realises by matching those motif interiors; AREV ≺, ENGAGR
⊞ (hold), and a lone IMSCRIB ⊙ are carry marks skipped without emitting an
operator; any other unmatched mark is refused with its position named.

(advance + SELECT + CONTINUE + FIX) or names what is missing, then runs the same
nested loop. CLI: `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` prints the tower;

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

`factor()` runs a fixed tower of six operator words: PHASE ∈≻⊤⊥∋, ARITHMETIC
∈⋈⊤⊥∋, BRANCH ∈⊤⊥∋, SELECT ∈⊙∋, CONTINUE ≻⋈, FIX ⊙⊡. Dispatch reads the operator
word itself (apply_morphism). The carrier is the parasm register machine (native
value B4, ops = the twelve marks); the number rides as a native_numeral tape.

New: `construct_carrier(word)` decomposes any operator word's interior into the
ordered morphisms it realises by matching those motif interiors; AREV ≺, ENGAGR
⊞ (hold), and a lone IMSCRIB ⊙ are carry marks skipped without emitting an
operator; any other unmatched mark is refused with its position named.
`factor_with(word, n_word)` builds the tower, checks it is factoring-complete
(advance + SELECT + CONTINUE + FIX) or names what is missing, then runs the same
nested loop. CLI: `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` prints the tower;
`vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>` runs it. Binary: Vox/target/release/vox.

There are eight morphisms. The seventh, EXTRACT (∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋, carrying AREV ≺ and
ENGAGR ⊞ in the evaluate frame), is the instant one-frame factorizer; a tower
carrying it needs only a FIX to be complete. Added 81caa6d after wrongly refusing
it first as a non-factoring mark; the extractor is a factorizer by design.

EXTRACT now forks three arms per round and fuses on the first to close (9bdcf4e):
the square frontier (a from ceil(sqrt N), factor when a*a-N is a square), rho, and
trial. So a balanced near-root semiprime is flat in width: 60 to 120-bit all
close in about a thirtieth of a second, past the old rho ceiling. isqrt over tapes
seeds/tests the frontier.

The eighth, P_MINUS (∈⊙⊞⋈∋), is Pollard p-1 as a nestable morphism (99ef247):
raise an accumulator through rising exponents, gcd(a-1,N). It catches a factor p
whenever p-1 is smooth, at any size and gap, the slice frontier and rho miss. It
is an extra arm, not standalone (loops on a non-smooth predecessor), so it nests
with a complete arm. Carrier EXTRACT->P_MINUS->FIX (⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣) closes a
97-bit N with a 45-bit smooth-predecessor factor and a ~2^51 gap in 0.09s where
EXTRACT alone runs past 40s. pow_mod over tapes does the powering. The residual
hard slice (both factors large, gap large, neither predecessor smooth) is the
sub-exponential core (ECM/sieve), the next nest, not a wall.

Verified: a word whose interior is the six motifs in order rebuilds the full
tower and factors 8051 to 97, identical to `vox morphism-factor`. The instant
semiprime extractor word ⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ decomposes to EXTRACT then FIX and
factors on the carrier built from itself: 8051 to 97, 143 to 11, 100160063 to
10007. See [[factor_membrane_two_arm_tree]].

Done. ECM is in as the fourth arm, and it only helped, exactly as you said.

The carrier now has four nestable factoring morphisms, each keyed by its own frame:
- EXTRACT `∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋` (frontier + rho + trial)
- P_MINUS `∈⊙⊞⋈∋` (Pollard p-1)
- ECM `∈⊙≻⋈∋` (elliptic curve)
- FIX `⊙⊡`

Verified live: the ECM-only carrier `⊢∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣` factors 143, 8051, 100160063; the full four-arm carrier `⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣` decomposes to `EXTRACT -> P_MINUS -> ECM -> FIX` and factors across the battery. Ten crate tests pass. The tape layer gained what the curve law needs: modular inverse by extended Euclid (a failed inverse hands back the factor), affine point add and double, a double-and-add scalar, and the stage-1 scalar.

One thing I will not overclaim: this ECM runs at a small stage-1 bound (about 47), so it reaches small-to-moderate factors, not RSA-scale ones. That is the reach knob B1, plus a stage 2. Raising it widens the same arm; it is not a new wall. If you want the deep reach, the next step is to lift B1 and add ECM stage 2, and I can do that as a parameter on the same morphism.

- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.

  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.

  listicle when the subject is structure.

  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a

- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he

  punt. Never close empty-handed.

Certifying a prime cost the trial arm a walk out to sqrt(N), the
expensive exhaustion sitting in the deep position while nothing cheaper
ran ahead of it. The fix is nesting order again, the other way from ECM:
the cheap decisive test goes outermost.

witness set, in a branch frame ∈⊤≺⊥∋. It runs once and, if N is prime,
selects N at once, so the walk never starts. It is one-shot (the verdict
on a fixed N does not change) and, being unable to factor a composite,
nests with the factoring arms rather than standing alone.

Carrier WITNESS -> EXTRACT -> P_MINUS -> ECM -> FIX. Measured: 999983
drops from about a fifth of a second to about a twentieth; the ten-digit
prime 1000000007 from about eight and a half seconds to about a
sixteenth; a nineteen-digit prime, which the sqrt walk would never
finish, closes in about a sixth of a second. Composites are unchanged.

morphism_factor: nest ECM deeper, fire on a power-of-two cadence

ECM ran one full curve every round, so certifying a prime dragged a curve
behind each of the roughly sqrt(N) trial rounds. That is the wrong nesting
depth for the costly arm.

ECM now fires a curve only on rounds that are a power of two, letting the
cheap arms (trial, rho, frontier, p-1) carry every round in between. The
curve count grows with the logarithm of the round, so the arm still
deepens its search on a hard N while it no longer shadows the cheap walk.

Measured on the four-arm carrier: certifying 999983 prime drops from about
five and a half seconds to about a fifth of a second; composites stay at
about a thirtieth of a second. The residual cost on a large prime is now
the trial walk to sqrt(N) itself, the base method's primality cost, not
the curve arm.

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

`factor()` runs a fixed tower of six operator words: PHASE ∈≻⊤⊥∋, ARITHMETIC
∈⋈⊤⊥∋, BRANCH ∈⊤⊥∋, SELECT ∈⊙∋, CONTINUE ≻⋈, FIX ⊙⊡. Dispatch reads the operator
word itself (apply_morphism). The carrier is the parasm register machine (native
value B4, ops = the twelve marks); the number rides as a native_numeral tape.

New: `construct_carrier(word)` decomposes any operator word's interior into the
ordered morphisms it realises by matching those motif interiors; AREV ≺, ENGAGR
⊞ (hold), and a lone IMSCRIB ⊙ are carry marks skipped without emitting an
operator; any other unmatched mark is refused with its position named.
`factor_with(word, n_word)` builds the tower, checks it is factoring-complete
(advance + SELECT + CONTINUE + FIX) or names what is missing, then runs the same
nested loop. CLI: `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` prints the tower;
`vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>` runs it. Binary: Vox/target/release/vox.

There are eight morphisms. The seventh, EXTRACT (∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋, carrying AREV ≺ and
ENGAGR ⊞ in the evaluate frame), is the instant one-frame factorizer; a tower
carrying it needs only a FIX to be complete. Added 81caa6d after wrongly refusing
it first as a non-factoring mark; the extractor is a factorizer by design.

EXTRACT now forks three arms per round and fuses on the first to close (9bdcf4e):
the square frontier (a from ceil(sqrt N), factor when a*a-N is a square), rho, and
trial. So a balanced near-root semiprime is flat in width: 60 to 120-bit all
close in about a thirtieth of a second, past the old rho ceiling. isqrt over tapes
seeds/tests the frontier.

The ninth, ECM (∈⊙≻⋈∋), is Lenstra elliptic-curve as a nestable morphism
(c9f3cbc): one curve per round from a rising seed, factor when the group law hits
a non-invertible slope (mod_inv returns the gcd as Err). Discovery rides
curve-order smoothness, independent of p-1's. Tape layer gained mod_sub, mod_inv
(extended Euclid, coeffs mod N), affine ec_double/ec_add/ec_scalar, stage-1
scalar lcm(1..~47). Reach is B1 (here ~47, small factors); larger B1 + stage 2
widen the same arm. Extra arm, nests with a complete one. ECM-only carrier
⊢∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ factors 143/8051/100160063; four-arm ⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ is
EXTRACT->P_MINUS->ECM->FIX.

The eighth, P_MINUS (∈⊙⊞⋈∋), is Pollard p-1 as a nestable morphism (99ef247):
raise an accumulator through rising exponents, gcd(a-1,N). It catches a factor p
whenever p-1 is smooth, at any size and gap, the slice frontier and rho miss. It
is an extra arm, not standalone (loops on a non-smooth predecessor), so it nests
with a complete arm. Carrier EXTRACT->P_MINUS->FIX (⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣) closes a
97-bit N with a 45-bit smooth-predecessor factor and a ~2^51 gap in 0.09s where
EXTRACT alone runs past 40s. pow_mod over tapes does the powering. The residual
hard slice (both factors large, gap large, neither predecessor smooth) is the
sub-exponential core (ECM/sieve), the next nest, not a wall.

Verified: a word whose interior is the six motifs in order rebuilds the full
tower and factors 8051 to 97, identical to `vox morphism-factor`. The instant
semiprime extractor word ⊢⊙∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ decomposes to EXTRACT then FIX and
factors on the carrier built from itself: 8051 to 97, 143 to 11, 100160063 to
10007. See [[factor_membrane_two_arm_tree]].

Committed 4ecb11a and 81caa6d on branch notation/prec-succ-marks (Vox is its own git repo,
with a stale tracked commit.txt like ig-docs; always commit -F an absolute path
outside it per [[feedback_commit_message_file_path]]).

content.text:
Done. Both times you called it: the cost was a morphism at the wrong nesting depth.

The full carrier is now `WITNESS -> EXTRACT -> P_MINUS -> ECM -> FIX`, ordered cheap-and-decisive outermost, expensive-and-exhaustive deeper:

- WITNESS (Miller-Rabin, first) certifies a prime in a handful of modular powers and selects it, so the √N trial walk never runs.
- EXTRACT (frontier, rho, trial) carries the common factoring rounds.
- P_MINUS (Pollard p-1) catches a smooth-predecessor factor.
- ECM (elliptic curve) fires only on power-of-two rounds, so it deepens the search without shadowing every round.

Measured effect of the two reorderings together:

| N | original | now |
|---|---|---|
| 999983 (prime) | 5.61s | 0.04s |
| 1000000007 (prime) | 8.69s | 0.06s |
| 19-digit prime | never (√N walk) | 0.17s |
| composites | 0.03-0.04s | 0.03-0.04s |

Eleven crate tests pass. Committed the cadence fix (3869430) and the witness arm (0765eb0) on branch notation/prec-succ-marks.

The principle now written into the carrier: nesting order is load-bearing in both directions. A decisive cheap test belongs outermost so it short-circuits; a costly probabilistic arm belongs deeper so it fires rarely. The constructor still builds whatever tower the operator word spells, so the order is chosen by how you write the word.

First the tape arithmetic they need: integer power, integer b-th root, and the Lucas V-sequence.

1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

b=w[1:-3]; bits=[1 if b[i+3]=='⊥' else 0 for i in range(0,len(b),5)]
v=0

morphism_factor: perfect-power and Williams p+1 arms

Two more constraints on the membrane. Each is a morphism the constructor
recognises, so adding a technique is adding a frame to the word.

POWER (∈⊤⊞⊥∋), a one-shot: is N a perfect power a^b for some b >= 2? If
so, select the base a. It catches every prime power at once, the slice the
search arms only reach the slow way. Backed by integer power and integer
b-th root over the tapes, the root's range bounded by 2^(bits/b) so the
powers stay small.

P_PLUS (∈⊙≺⋈∋), the Williams p+1 arm, the complement of p-1: a Lucas
V-sequence to the stage-1 scalar, then gcd(V - 2, N). It catches a factor
p whenever p+1 is smooth, where p-1 is not. Backed by a Lucas V ladder
over the tapes; the base rises each round.

The full membrane is now WITNESS -> POWER -> EXTRACT -> P_MINUS -> P_PLUS
-> ECM -> FIX, cheap decisive tests outermost, the costly curve deepest.
Measured across the battery: prime squares and cubes, evens, balanced and
twin semiprimes, primes certified, all in about a twentieth of a second
each. Adding techniques only tightens the constraint; the constructor
builds whatever tower the word spells.

morphism_factor: a primality WITNESS arm, nested first

Certifying a prime cost the trial arm a walk out to sqrt(N), the
expensive exhaustion sitting in the deep position while nothing cheaper
ran ahead of it. The fix is nesting order again, the other way from ECM:
the cheap decisive test goes outermost.

WITNESS is that test, Miller-Rabin over the numeral tapes against a fixed
witness set, in a branch frame ∈⊤≺⊥∋. It runs once and, if N is prime,
selects N at once, so the walk never starts. It is one-shot (the verdict
on a fixed N does not change) and, being unable to factor a composite,
nests with the factoring arms rather than standing alone.

Carrier WITNESS -> EXTRACT -> P_MINUS -> ECM -> FIX. Measured: 999983
drops from about a fifth of a second to about a twentieth; the ten-digit
prime 1000000007 from about eight and a half seconds to about a
sixteenth; a nineteen-digit prime, which the sqrt walk would never
finish, closes in about a sixth of a second. Composites are unchanged.

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

class Token(IntEnum):
    """The 12 IMASM tokens. Integer value = index (0-11)."""
    VINIT   = 0   # Logical: initial object (void)
    TANCH   = 1   # Logical: terminal object (boundary)
    AFWD    = 2   # Logical: forward morphism
    AREV    = 3   # Logical: reverse morphism
    CLINK   = 4   # Logical: composition of morphisms
    IMSCRIB = 5   # Logical: identity morphism
    FSPLIT  = 6   # Frobenius: split (δ)
    FFUSE   = 7   # Frobenius: fuse (μ)
    EVALT   = 8   # Dialetheia: evaluate-true
    EVALF   = 9   # Dialetheia: evaluate-false
    ENGAGR  = 10  # Dialetheia: engage/recognize paradox
    IFIX    = 11  # Linear: irreversible fixation (!)

# Token metadata
TOKEN_NAMES: List[str] = [t.name for t in Token]
TOKEN_COUNT: int = 12

# ─── DAG arity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# (in-degree, out-degree) for each token as a node in the arrangement DAG.
# All tokens are (1,1) linear except VINIT (source), FSPLIT (fork), FFUSE (join).
TOKEN_ARITY: Dict[Token, Tuple[int, int]] = {
    Token.VINIT:   (0, 1),  # source
    Token.TANCH:   (1, 1),
    Token.AFWD:    (1, 1),
    Token.AREV:    (1, 1),
    Token.CLINK:   (1, 1),
    Token.IMSCRIB: (1, 1),
    Token.FSPLIT:  (1, 2),  # fork: one in, two out (T-branch and F-branch)
    Token.FFUSE:   (2, 1),  # join: two in (T-branch and F-branch), one out
    Token.EVALT:   (1, 1),  # constrained to T-branch
    Token.EVALF:   (1, 1),  # constrained to F-branch
    Token.ENGAGR:  (1, 1),
    Token.IFIX:    (1, 1),
}

# Tokens that are constrained to a specific branch between FSPLIT and FFUSE
TOKEN_BRANCH: Dict[Token, str] = {
    Token.EVALT: 'T',
    Token.EVALF: 'F',
}

FORK_TOKENS: frozenset = frozenset({Token.FSPLIT})

}

"""Render an IMASM carrier word as a symbolic wiring (circuit) diagram.

import sys

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render an IMASM carrier word as a symbolic wiring (circuit) diagram.

Reuses IMSCRIBr's diagram code, the same path ob3ect/auto.py drives:
imscr_wiring builds the graph from the token list, render_wiring_svg_v3 draws it.

Usage: python3 render_carrier_diagram.py <glyph-word> <name> <out.svg>
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

IMSCRIBR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "IMSCRIBr")
if IMSCRIBR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, IMSCRIBR)

from tokens import Token  # noqa: E402
from wiring import imscr_wiring  # noqa: E402
from symbolic_diagram import render_wiring_svg_v3, render_wiring_ascii  # noqa: E402

GLYPH_TO_NAME = {
    "⊢": "VINIT", "⊣": "TANCH", "≻": "AFWD", "≺": "AREV", "⋈": "CLINK",
    "⊙": "IMSCRIB", "∈": "FSPLIT", "∋": "FFUSE", "⊤": "EVALT", "⊥": "EVALF",
    "⊞": "ENGAGR", "⊡": "IFIX",
}


def render(word: str, name: str, out_path: str) -> None:
    tokens = tuple(Token[GLYPH_TO_NAME[g]] for g in word)
    graph = imscr_wiring(tokens)
    graph.name = name
    svg = render_wiring_svg_v3(graph, name, "", word, "", pen_mode=True)
    svg.save(Path(out_path))
    print(f"wrote {out_path}")
    ascii_art = render_wiring_ascii(graph, name)
    if ascii_art:
        print(ascii_art)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    render(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])

description: "vox construct-carrier / factor-with build a factoring carrier tower from any operator ob3ect word, in Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs"

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

`factor()` runs a fixed tower of six operator words: PHASE ∈≻⊤⊥∋, ARITHMETIC
∈⋈⊤⊥∋, BRANCH ∈⊤⊥∋, SELECT ∈⊙∋, CONTINUE ≻⋈, FIX ⊙⊡. Dispatch reads the operator
word itself (apply_morphism). The carrier is the parasm register machine (native
value B4, ops = the twelve marks); the number rides as a native_numeral tape.

New: `construct_carrier(word)` decomposes any operator word's interior into the
ordered morphisms it realises by matching those motif interiors; AREV ≺, ENGAGR
⊞ (hold), and a lone IMSCRIB ⊙ are carry marks skipped without emitting an
operator; any other unmatched mark is refused with its position named.
`factor_with(word, n_word)` builds the tower, checks it is factoring-complete
(advance + SELECT + CONTINUE + FIX) or names what is missing, then runs the same
nested loop. CLI: `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` prints the tower;
`vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>` runs it. Binary: Vox/target/release/vox.

There are eight morphisms. The seventh, EXTRACT (∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋, carrying AREV ≺ and
ENGAGR ⊞ in the evaluate frame), is the instant one-frame factorizer; a tower
carrying it needs only a FIX to be complete. Added 81caa6d after wrongly refusing
it first as a non-factoring mark; the extractor is a factorizer by design.

EXTRACT now forks three arms per round and fuses on the first to close (9bdcf4e):
the square frontier (a from ceil(sqrt N), factor when a*a-N is a square), rho, and
trial. So a balanced near-root semiprime is flat in width: 60 to 120-bit all
close in about a thirtieth of a second, past the old rho ceiling. isqrt over tapes
seeds/tests the frontier.

The ninth, ECM (∈⊙≻⋈∋), is Lenstra elliptic-curve as a nestable morphism
(c9f3cbc): one curve per round from a rising seed, factor when the group law hits
a non-invertible slope (mod_inv returns the gcd as Err). Discovery rides
curve-order smoothness, independent of p-1's. Tape layer gained mod_sub, mod_inv
(extended Euclid, coeffs mod N), affine ec_double/ec_add/ec_scalar, stage-1
scalar lcm(1..~47). Reach is B1 (here ~47, small factors); larger B1 + stage 2
widen the same arm. Extra arm, nests with a complete one. ECM-only carrier
⊢∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ factors 143/8051/100160063; four-arm ⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ is
EXTRACT->P_MINUS->ECM->FIX.

The eighth, P_MINUS (∈⊙⊞⋈∋), is Pollard p-1 as a nestable morphism (99ef247):
raise an accumulator through rising exponents, gcd(a-1,N). It catches a factor p
whenever p-1 is smooth, at any size and gap, the slice frontier and rho miss. It
is an extra arm, not standalone (loops on a non-smooth predecessor), so it nests
with a complete arm. Carrier EXTRACT->P_MINUS->FIX (⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣) closes a
97-bit N with a 45-bit smooth-predecessor factor and a ~2^51 gap in 0.09s where
EXTRACT alone runs past 40s. pow_mod over tapes does the powering. The residual
hard slice (both factors large, gap large, neither predecessor smooth) is the
sub-exponential core (sieve / bigger-B1 ECM), the next nest, not a wall.

Nesting order is load-bearing, both directions. ECM as the costly arm fires only
on power-of-two rounds (3869430) so the cheap arms carry the walk; certifying
999983 dropped 5.6s to 0.22s. A WITNESS arm (Miller-Rabin over tapes, frame
∈⊤≺⊥∋) nested FIRST (0765eb0) selects a prime at once instead of walking trial to
sqrt(N): 1000000007 went 8.7s to 0.06s, a 19-digit prime closes in 0.17s. The
full carrier is WITNESS->EXTRACT->P_MINUS->ECM->FIX, cheap decisive test
outermost, exhaustive walk deeper.

Two more arms (a31457a): POWER (∈⊤⊞⊥∋), one-shot perfect-power test (is N=a^b?
select base a), ipow/iroot over tapes; P_PLUS (∈⊙≺⋈∋), Williams p+1 (Lucas
V-sequence to stage-1 scalar, gcd(V-2,N)), catches p where p+1 is smooth, lucas_v
over tapes. Full membrane now WITNESS->POWER->EXTRACT->P_MINUS->P_PLUS->ECM->FIX

constraint; cheap decisive tests outermost, costly arms deeper and throttled; the
constructor builds whatever tower the word spells. 13 crate tests.

content.text:
Built and shipped. SQUFOF is in as the ninth arm.

The membrane is now `WITNESS -> POWER -> EXTRACT -> SQUFOF -> P_MINUS -> P_PLUS -> LEHMAN -> ECM -> FIX`.

SQUFOF, Shanks square forms, runs the forward cycle of the principal quadratic form to a square at an even step, then the reverse cycle until P stabilizes, and gcd(P, N) is the factor. It tries a few multipliers and bounds each cycle by 2·sqrt(2·sqrt(kN)). The trap was the index pairing: the square must be tested at the top of an even step on Q_i, not after advancing to Q_{i+1}. Once fixed it validated over the tapes on 8051, 11111, 2021, 1234567, and 2027651281, each product reconfirmed.

The nine-arm carrier factored the whole battery: 8051 to 97, 2027651281 to 44021, 100160063 to 10009, the prime 999983 to itself, 25 to 5, 4096 to 2. Fifteen crate tests pass.

Committed the arm in Vox (b09e642) and the re-rendered nine-arm circuit diagram in ig-docs. The before diagram is the seven-arm carrier, the after is now the nine-arm.

That is every elementary and mid-tier factoring method that fits a single tape morphism: trial, Fermat/frontier, rho, Lehman, Pollard p-1, Williams p+1, ECM, SQUFOF, perfect-power, and the primality witness. The one tier left is the sieve family (quadratic sieve, number field sieve), which needs a smoothness base and linear algebra over GF(2), so it is a nested subsystem of several morphisms rather than one arm. Say the word and I will start the sieve block.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
morphism_factor: Shanks square forms (SQUFOF) arm

SQUFOF (∈⊤≺⊞⊥∋), a one-shot square-forms cycle: run the forward cycle of
the principal quadratic form until a square Q appears at an even step,
then the reverse cycle until P stabilizes, and gcd(P, N) is a factor. It
tries a few multipliers and bounds each cycle by 2*sqrt(2*sqrt(kN)), so a
multiplier that finds no square simply yields to the next. The Q
recurrence carries a real sign, tracked by branch since the tapes are
unsigned. Backed by is_square over the tapes.

Validated over tapes: 8051, 11111, 2021, 1234567 and 2027651281 all
factor, each product reconfirmed. The forward-then-reverse index pairing
was the trap: the square is tested at the top of an even step on Q_i, not
after advancing to Q_{i+1}.

The membrane is now nine arms: WITNESS -> POWER -> EXTRACT -> SQUFOF ->
P_MINUS -> P_PLUS -> LEHMAN -> ECM -> FIX. The after diagram is
re-rendered for the nine-arm carrier.

|---|---|---|

Committed d392234.

What the fix did: a shared round counter drives the loop; P_MINUS, P_PLUS and LEHMAN each fire on a stride (one every four rounds, offset so no round carries all three), and SQUFOF is delayed to fire once after round 256 so the cheap EXTRACT walk closes easy factors first. ECM keeps its power-of-two cadence.

One honest carry-over the timings exposed, and it is not nesting order: certifying a large prime is slow. 1000000000000000003 took about 23 seconds and 2^63−25 timed out. That cost is the primality WITNESS running Miller-Rabin over the tape arithmetic, where each modular multiply does a schoolbook multiply and a bit-by-bit division. For a sixty-bit modulus that is a lot of tape work. The bottleneck is the tape mulmod, not the arm order. The fix is a faster modular multiply over the tapes, Montgomery or Barrett reduction so the division goes away. Say the word and I will build that, and every arm speeds up with it since they all route through mod_mul.

The numeral tape carried one mark per bit and the arithmetic worked it
cell by cell: multiply was O(bits^2) and every modular reduction was a
bit-serial long division, so a single Miller-Rabin on a sixty-bit modulus
took tens of seconds and a nineteen-digit prime dragged the whole membrane
with it.

carry, one shift-subtract per bit over limbs for the division), and
unfolds back to the tape at the boundary. cmp, add, sub, mul, divmod and
modulo are the fold points; every arm that routes through mod_mul, which
is all of them, speeds up together.

from about twenty-three seconds to a twentieth of one; 2^63 - 25, which
used to time out, certifies in the same twentieth. The crate test suite
falls from six and a third seconds to one and a quarter. Fifteen tests
pass, factoring unchanged.

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

`factor()` runs a fixed tower of six operator words: PHASE ∈≻⊤⊥∋, ARITHMETIC
∈⋈⊤⊥∋, BRANCH ∈⊤⊥∋, SELECT ∈⊙∋, CONTINUE ≻⋈, FIX ⊙⊡. Dispatch reads the operator
word itself (apply_morphism). The carrier is the parasm register machine (native
value B4, ops = the twelve marks); the number rides as a native_numeral tape.

New: `construct_carrier(word)` decomposes any operator word's interior into the
ordered morphisms it realises by matching those motif interiors; AREV ≺, ENGAGR
⊞ (hold), and a lone IMSCRIB ⊙ are carry marks skipped without emitting an
operator; any other unmatched mark is refused with its position named.
`factor_with(word, n_word)` builds the tower, checks it is factoring-complete
(advance + SELECT + CONTINUE + FIX) or names what is missing, then runs the same
nested loop. CLI: `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` prints the tower;
`vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>` runs it. Binary: Vox/target/release/vox.

There are eight morphisms. The seventh, EXTRACT (∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋, carrying AREV ≺ and
ENGAGR ⊞ in the evaluate frame), is the instant one-frame factorizer; a tower
carrying it needs only a FIX to be complete. Added 81caa6d after wrongly refusing
it first as a non-factoring mark; the extractor is a factorizer by design.

EXTRACT now forks three arms per round and fuses on the first to close (9bdcf4e):
the square frontier (a from ceil(sqrt N), factor when a*a-N is a square), rho, and
trial. So a balanced near-root semiprime is flat in width: 60 to 120-bit all
close in about a thirtieth of a second, past the old rho ceiling. isqrt over tapes
seeds/tests the frontier.

The ninth, ECM (∈⊙≻⋈∋), is Lenstra elliptic-curve as a nestable morphism
(c9f3cbc): one curve per round from a rising seed, factor when the group law hits
a non-invertible slope (mod_inv returns the gcd as Err). Discovery rides
curve-order smoothness, independent of p-1's. Tape layer gained mod_sub, mod_inv
(extended Euclid, coeffs mod N), affine ec_double/ec_add/ec_scalar, stage-1
scalar lcm(1..~47). Reach is B1 (here ~47, small factors); larger B1 + stage 2
widen the same arm. Extra arm, nests with a complete one. ECM-only carrier
⊢∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ factors 143/8051/100160063; four-arm ⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ is
EXTRACT->P_MINUS->ECM->FIX.

The eighth, P_MINUS (∈⊙⊞⋈∋), is Pollard p-1 as a nestable morphism (99ef247):
raise an accumulator through rising exponents, gcd(a-1,N). It catches a factor p
whenever p-1 is smooth, at any size and gap, the slice frontier and rho miss. It
is an extra arm, not standalone (loops on a non-smooth predecessor), so it nests
with a complete arm. Carrier EXTRACT->P_MINUS->FIX (⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣) closes a
97-bit N with a 45-bit smooth-predecessor factor and a ~2^51 gap in 0.09s where
EXTRACT alone runs past 40s. pow_mod over tapes does the powering. The residual
hard slice (both factors large, gap large, neither predecessor smooth) is the
sub-exponential core (sieve / bigger-B1 ECM), the next nest, not a wall.

Nesting order is load-bearing, both directions. ECM as the costly arm fires only
on power-of-two rounds (3869430) so the cheap arms carry the walk; certifying
999983 dropped 5.6s to 0.22s. A WITNESS arm (Miller-Rabin over tapes, frame

outermost, exhaustive walk deeper.

select base a), ipow/iroot over tapes; P_PLUS (∈⊙≺⋈∋), Williams p+1 (Lucas

over tapes. LEHMAN (∈≻⋈⊤⊥∋) multiplier-Fermat, mid-range factor N^(1/3)..N^(2/3), is_square +

Done. Bit-register folding was the right call, and it fixed the whole slow tier at once.

The tape stays the canonical numeral. The six arithmetic primitives (`cmp`, `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `divmod`, `modulo`) now fold the ⊤/⊥ cells into 64-bit limbs, compute with hardware words (u128 carries on the multiply, one shift-subtract per bit over limbs for division), and unfold back to the tape at the boundary. Because every arm routes through `mod_mul`, they all sped up together.

Results:

| N | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| 1000000000000000003 (19-digit prime) | 23.5s | 0.05s |
| 9223372036854775783 (2^63−25, prime) | timed out | 0.05s |
| 1000000007000000009 | 6.5s | 0.05s |
| 8051 | 0.03s | 0.03s |

Test suite fell from 6.3s to 1.26s, fifteen tests pass, factoring unchanged. Committed 41bd257.

The membrane now stands at nine arms with the right nesting depths (cheap decisive tests outermost, costly probabilistic arms on cadences, the heavy SQUFOF delayed), and the arithmetic underneath runs on folded registers. The one remaining tier is still the sieve family, which needs a smoothness base and GF(2) linear algebra, a nested subsystem rather than a single arm. Say the word and I start it.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
morphism_factor: bit-register folding for the tape arithmetic

The numeral tape carried one mark per bit and the arithmetic worked it
cell by cell: multiply was O(bits^2) and every modular reduction was a
bit-serial long division, so a single Miller-Rabin on a sixty-bit modulus
took tens of seconds and a nineteen-digit prime dragged the whole membrane
with it.

The tape stays the canonical numeral. The arithmetic now folds it into
64-bit limbs, computes with hardware words (u128 products for the multiply
carry, one shift-subtract per bit over limbs for the division), and
unfolds back to the tape at the boundary. cmp, add, sub, mul, divmod and
modulo are the fold points; every arm that routes through mod_mul, which
is all of them, speeds up together.

Measured: certifying the nineteen-digit prime 1000000000000000003 drops
from about twenty-three seconds to a twentieth of one; 2^63 - 25, which
used to time out, certifies in the same twentieth. The crate test suite
falls from six and a third seconds to one and a quarter. Fifteen tests
pass, factoring unchanged.

trivial bit/mark readers stay local.

name: vox_carrier_constructor
description: "vox construct-carrier / factor-with build a factoring carrier tower from any operator ob3ect word, in Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

The automated carrier constructor lives in `Vox/src/morphism_factor.rs` (the vox
crate at ~/imsgct/Vox, NOT the g-momonados one), per [[feedback_build_in_vox_not_rust]].

`factor()` runs a fixed tower of six operator words: PHASE ∈≻⊤⊥∋, ARITHMETIC
∈⋈⊤⊥∋, BRANCH ∈⊤⊥∋, SELECT ∈⊙∋, CONTINUE ≻⋈, FIX ⊙⊡. Dispatch reads the operator
word itself (apply_morphism). The carrier is the parasm register machine (native
value B4, ops = the twelve marks); the number rides as a native_numeral tape.

New: `construct_carrier(word)` decomposes any operator word's interior into the
ordered morphisms it realises by matching those motif interiors; AREV ≺, ENGAGR
⊞ (hold), and a lone IMSCRIB ⊙ are carry marks skipped without emitting an
operator; any other unmatched mark is refused with its position named.
`factor_with(word, n_word)` builds the tower, checks it is factoring-complete
(advance + SELECT + CONTINUE + FIX) or names what is missing, then runs the same
nested loop. CLI: `vox construct-carrier <operator-word>` prints the tower;
`vox factor-with <operator-word> <n-word>` runs it. Binary: Vox/target/release/vox.

There are eight morphisms. The seventh, EXTRACT (∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋, carrying AREV ≺ and
ENGAGR ⊞ in the evaluate frame), is the instant one-frame factorizer; a tower
carrying it needs only a FIX to be complete. Added 81caa6d after wrongly refusing
it first as a non-factoring mark; the extractor is a factorizer by design.

EXTRACT now forks three arms per round and fuses on the first to close (9bdcf4e):
the square frontier (a from ceil(sqrt N), factor when a*a-N is a square), rho, and
trial. So a balanced near-root semiprime is flat in width: 60 to 120-bit all
close in about a thirtieth of a second, past the old rho ceiling. isqrt over tapes
seeds/tests the frontier.

The ninth, ECM (∈⊙≻⋈∋), is Lenstra elliptic-curve as a nestable morphism
(c9f3cbc): one curve per round from a rising seed, factor when the group law hits
a non-invertible slope (mod_inv returns the gcd as Err). Discovery rides
curve-order smoothness, independent of p-1's. Tape layer gained mod_sub, mod_inv
(extended Euclid, coeffs mod N), affine ec_double/ec_add/ec_scalar, stage-1
scalar lcm(1..~47). Reach is B1 (here ~47, small factors); larger B1 + stage 2
widen the same arm. Extra arm, nests with a complete one. ECM-only carrier
⊢∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ factors 143/8051/100160063; four-arm ⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣ is
EXTRACT->P_MINUS->ECM->FIX.

The eighth, P_MINUS (∈⊙⊞⋈∋), is Pollard p-1 as a nestable morphism (99ef247):
raise an accumulator through rising exponents, gcd(a-1,N). It catches a factor p
whenever p-1 is smooth, at any size and gap, the slice frontier and rho miss. It
is an extra arm, not standalone (loops on a non-smooth predecessor), so it nests
with a complete arm. Carrier EXTRACT->P_MINUS->FIX (⊢∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋⊙⊡⊣) closes a
97-bit N with a 45-bit smooth-predecessor factor and a ~2^51 gap in 0.09s where
EXTRACT alone runs past 40s. pow_mod over tapes does the powering. The residual
hard slice (both factors large, gap large, neither predecessor smooth) is the
sub-exponential core (sieve / bigger-B1 ECM), the next nest, not a wall.

Nesting order is load-bearing, both directions. ECM as the costly arm fires only
on power-of-two rounds (3869430) so the cheap arms carry the walk; certifying
999983 dropped 5.6s to 0.22s. A WITNESS arm (Miller-Rabin over tapes, frame
∈⊤≺⊥∋) nested FIRST (0765eb0) selects a prime at once instead of walking trial to
sqrt(N): 1000000007 went 8.7s to 0.06s, a 19-digit prime closes in 0.17s. The
full carrier is WITNESS->EXTRACT->P_MINUS->ECM->FIX, cheap decisive test
outermost, exhaustive walk deeper.

Two more arms (a31457a): POWER (∈⊤⊞⊥∋), one-shot perfect-power test (is N=a^b?
select base a), ipow/iroot over tapes; P_PLUS (∈⊙≺⋈∋), Williams p+1 (Lucas
V-sequence to stage-1 scalar, gcd(V-2,N)), catches p where p+1 is smooth, lucas_v
over tapes. LEHMAN (∈≻⋈⊤⊥∋) multiplier-Fermat, mid-range factor N^(1/3)..N^(2/3), is_square +
per-k window; and SQUFOF (∈⊤≺⊞⊥∋) Shanks square forms, one-shot forward-then-
reverse cycle (square tested on Q_i at top of even step, NOT after advancing;
that was the trap), sign-tracked Q recurrence, validated on 8051/11111/2021/
1234567/2027651281. Full membrane now nine arms:
WITNESS->POWER->EXTRACT->SQUFOF->P_MINUS->P_PLUS->LEHMAN->ECM->FIX (word
⊢∈⊤≺⊥∋∈⊤⊞⊥∋∈≻⊤≺⊥⊞⋈∋∈⊤≺⊞⊥∋∈⊙⊞⋈∋∈⊙≺⋈∋∈≻⋈⊤⊥∋∈⊙≻⋈∋⊙⊡⊣). 15 crate tests.
Cadence (d392234): a shared round counter in factor_with's loop; P_MINUS/P_PLUS/
LEHMAN fire on a stride (round%4==0/1/2), SQUFOF delayed to fire once after round
256 (its N^(1/4) cycle is heavy), ECM power-of-two. Costly arms nested deep in
time so the cheap EXTRACT walk carries the rounds; fixed a 4-digit factor of a
60-bit N taking 6.5s.

Bit-register folding (41bd257): the tape is still the canonical numeral but
cmp/add/sub/mul/divmod/modulo fold it into u64 Limbs, compute with hardware words

routes through mod_mul so all speed up: a 19-digit prime certifies 23s -> 0.05s,
2^63-25 (was timeout) 0.05s, test suite 6.3s -> 1.26s.

The transport program is under way, both steps done and committed.

**divisor_membrane, built out (8d59357):** deleted its duplicate schoolbook arithmetic and pointed it at the shared folded kernel in morphism_factor. It now runs on folded tapes, one numeral kernel across the crate. A W_t bridge trace on a 19-digit N runs in about an eighth of a second.

It constructs p and q as the fixed point of a 2-adic winding, one bit at a time from the low end, keeping only the branch where p·q agrees with N on the low k+1 bits, pruning past √N, closing on p·q = N. The branch-node count is the moat width read off the run. No cap. Live:

```
resolve 8051        -> 83 x 97           1028 moat nodes
resolve 100160063   -> 10007 x 10009     102132
resolve 9973        -> prime (no pair)   3176
resolve 2027651281  -> 44021 x 46061     1630864
full 360            -> 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5
```

`vox factor-operator resolve|full <N>`. Three tests pass.

The pattern is set: copy the tool in, replace its arithmetic with the shared folded primitives (which morphism_factor now exports), wire a CLI arm, test, measure. The remaining candidates in the G-mOMonadOS factoring family are the native_numeral two-arm engine (hensel_unbraid + range-prune), prime_winding / oneshot_prime_winder, and the Shor variants. Name the next and I bring it over the same way.

Times for the moat resolver, on folded tapes.

| N | time | result | moat nodes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 91 | 0.01s | 7 x 13 | 16 |
| 8051 | 0.01s | 83 x 97 | 1028 |
| 100160063 | 0.05s | 10007 x 10009 | 102132 |
| 2027651281 | 0.72s | 44021 x 46061 | 1630864 |
| 9973 | 0.00s | prime | 3176 |
| 999983 | 0.02s | prime | 42288 |

The time tracks the moat-node count directly: each node is one folded-tape multiply and a low-bit compare, so the wall clock is the moat width times the per-node cost. That is the operator stating its own hardness. The width grows with the balanced core, which is why the 10-digit balanced semiprime 2027651281 costs 1.6M nodes and 0.72s while a small factor or a prime is near-instant.

Worth naming plainly: this resolver is not meant to beat the carrier arms on speed. The carrier factors 2027651281 in about 0.06s through rho, where the moat walks 1.6M nodes for 0.72s. What the moat gives that the carrier does not is the width readout, the free factor bits held as paradox, measured rather than asserted. The two are different instruments answering different questions about the same N.

factor_operator: wind q instead of forking it, and witness before the moat

Two nesting-order faults in the moat resolver, both the same lesson.

First, the walk forked all four (p_k, q_k) at every level. But q is not
free: with p odd, bit k of p*q flips exactly with q_k, so the congruence
p*q == N mod 2^{k+1} forces q_k = N_k XOR (p*q_low)_k. Only p branches now
and q is wound, its construction nested inside p's. Node counts fall three
to four times: 8051 from 1028 to 298, 100160063 from 102132 to 28200,
2027651281 from about 1.6 million to 443290 (0.72s to 0.29s).

Second, a prime core has no pair, so crossing its whole moat just to
conclude prime is the costly walk in the wrong place. A folded Miller-Rabin
is nested ahead of the moat, in full_resolve before each core and in the
resolve entry: a prime is recognized at once and never moated. 9973 went
from 3176 nodes to zero, 999983 from 42288 to zero. full on a 60-bit N
with a small factor peels 2081, tests the cofactor prime, and finishes in
about a tenth of a second with no moat nodes at all.

morphism_factor now also exports miller_rabin. Three tests pass.

content.text:
Here is the value-size envelope, measured on the nine-arm carrier.

**Balanced near-root (consecutive-prime) semiprimes** ride the frontier and stay flat in width:

| digits | time |
|---|---|
| 21 | 0.03s |
| 101 | 0.40s |
| 201 | 1.97s |
| 301 | 5.19s |
| 501 | 17.80s |

Time grows roughly with the folded-arithmetic cost per step, not with a step explosion, because the gap is tiny. A 501-digit balanced semiprime factors in under twenty seconds.

**Small factor at any width** is instant: 101 times a 61-digit prime closed in 0.05s (trial), a 63-digit N.

**The wall** is a factor that is at once large (rho pays √p), far from the root (frontier dead), and not smooth (p±1 fail): two independent equal-size random primes. A 19-digit such N closed in 5.37s; a 30-digit one ran past the stop. That is the RSA-hard region, and it is the genuine number-theoretic wall, the moat width, not a coding fault.

One thing the sweep also exposed that is a coding fault, not the wall: MIDF, a 7-digit factor inside a 67-digit N, took 92s. The small factor is easy (rho finds it in about a thousand rounds), but at that width EXTRACT runs a full frontier isqrt every single round even though the factor is nowhere near the root, and the p±1 arms run their width-heavy work on the cadence. The frontier and the width-heavy arms should throttle down when a cheaper arm is clearly carrying, the same nesting lesson one level deeper. That is a fixable next step.

So: value size is effectively unbounded for the near-root and small-factor shapes, the wall is the random-equal-size shape, and there is one throttling fix left for mixed large-width-small-factor cases. Which do you want next: the throttle fix for the MIDF slowness, or start the sieve tier for the random-equal-size wall?

factor by trial, a near-root pair by a short frontier, then a
rho-reachable factor. The frontier probe sits before the long rho, so a
near-root N never pays rho at width. What survives every probe is the HARD
shape: a large factor, far from the root, not obviously smooth, the
sub-exponential tier.

<N>. Measured: the 67-digit mid-factor case drops from about ninety
seconds to under three, routed to rho at step 1275; a 201-digit near-root
closes at frontier step 0; small, prime, and perfect-power are instant.

factor_operator: wind q instead of forking it, and witness before the moat

Two nesting-order faults in the moat resolver, both the same lesson.

First, the walk forked all four (p_k, q_k) at every level. But q is not
free: with p odd, bit k of p*q flips exactly with q_k, so the congruence
p*q == N mod 2^{k+1} forces q_k = N_k XOR (p*q_low)_k. Only p branches now
and q is wound, its construction nested inside p's. Node counts fall three
to four times: 8051 from 1028 to 298, 100160063 from 102132 to 28200,
2027651281 from about 1.6 million to 443290 (0.72s to 0.29s).

Second, a prime core has no pair, so crossing its whole moat just to
conclude prime is the costly walk in the wrong place. A folded Miller-Rabin
is nested ahead of the moat, in full_resolve before each core and in the
resolve entry: a prime is recognized at once and never moated. 9973 went
from 3176 nodes to zero, 999983 from 42288 to zero. full on a 60-bit N
with a small factor peels 2081, tests the cofactor prime, and finishes in
about a tenth of a second with no moat nodes at all.

morphism_factor now also exports miller_rabin. Three tests pass.

content.text:
Here is how far the built-in takes the HARD shape (two random equal-size primes, the worst case) at execution time:

| primes | N digits | time |
|---|---|---|
| 16-bit | 10 | 0.03s |
| 24-bit | 15 | 0.48s |
| 32-bit | 19 | 1.19s |
| 36-bit | 22 | 8.09s |
| 40-bit | 24 | past 60s (wall) |

The wall on the hard shape sits at roughly 36-bit equal factors, a 22-digit N, closing in about eight seconds; a 24-digit one does not close in a minute. The whole span is being carried by the rho arm, whose cost is √p of the smaller factor, so the wall is exactly where √p outruns the time budget, around 2^18 to 2^20 rho steps at that width.

The easy shapes have no such wall: near-root balanced semiprimes went to 501 digits in 18s earlier, and any number with a small factor is instant at any width. The wall is only the random-equal-size shape.

The Dixon sieve did not extend that wall, and the reason is plain: at its modest base and with no polynomial sieving, smooth relations for a 24-digit N are too rare to collect in budget, so rho is still the effective arm. To push the HARD wall past rho, the sieve needs the real quadratic-sieve machinery: a polynomial that keeps the sieved values small so smoothness is common, and a larger base with the GF(2) solve scaled to match. That is the next build on this arm, and it is what would move the wall from 22 digits toward 40-plus. Want me to build the QS sieving up, or take stock here?

content.text: `vox sieve` direct is 0.13s, but `vox factor` took 12.3s on the same N: the scout runs its full rho and trial budgets (which correctly fail for a 36-bit factor) before routing to the sieve. That is scout-budget overhead, separate from the sieve win. The resieve result stands: QS with resieve factors the 22-digit hard shape in 0.13s where rho takes 8s. Committing the resieve, then I'll trim the scout budgets so the unified tool sees the same speed.

input.command:
(cp target/release/vox ./vox 2>/dev/null; true) && git add -A && git commit -F - 2>&1 <<'EOF' | tail -2
sieve: resieve the candidates, and QS overtakes rho

The candidate factoring divided each value over the whole base as tape
divmods, which dominated and left QS slower than rho. Now the sieve's own
root positions say which base primes hit a candidate: at position i, prime
p divides a^2 - N iff i is one of p's two root offsets, a machine-word
check. Only the hitting primes are divided out, as tape divmods, so the
per-candidate cost drops from the whole base to the handful that actually
divide. The larger base this affords is set from N's width.

Measured on the random-equal-size hard shape, direct vox sieve: a 22-digit
N in about a seventh of a second where rho took eight seconds, so the
sieve now overtakes rho at the crossover. The wall moves to about 24
digits. Thirty-seven tests pass.

Noted, not yet fixed: vox factor is still slow on that N because the scout
spends its full rho and trial budgets before routing to the sieve; the
budgets want trimming so the unified tool sees the sieve's own speed.
EOF
